chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Boston, Miami, New York, Miami: unpaid travel days
summary: A booking run of Boston, two days to Miami, back to New York and Miami again paid only for working nights.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: They booked us out of New York one night to play Boston. We went to Boston and played, then we left there, in the bus, and our next engagement was in Miami, Florida. Now, we finished the night in Miami; our next engagement was in New York. One night. We played one night in New York, and back down to Miami again!

Now, it takes two days to travel down there in a bus. Well, see, if you were traveling two days that's on you, because when you don't work, you don't get paid. When you're traveling, that's on you. You get paid nothin' for traveling. So the only time we get paid was when we were working, playin' the dances. Well, we played a night in Boston, travel two days and go to Miami, and get paid for one night; travel two days back, get paid for one night; then back to Miami again. Well, I mean, when you stop to figure it out, with the time that you spent traveling, you kind of lost money on the deal. See, Louis wasn't the type of guy to come up and say, 'Well, boys, you did a good and keep this-that-or-the-other,' you know. If anybody did that, it was Joe Glaser. Which...that was him doing the dealing. No, the money was pretty...
